# Contributing Guide

This repository is a **pnpm monorepo** containing multiple SiYuan marketplace plugins (`packages/plugin/*`) and internal shared libraries (`packages/lib/*`). Plugin packages share a unified vite build (the factory in root `scripts/vite-plugin-config.ts`), with artifacts in each package's `dist/`.

## Repository Structure

```
packages/
├── plugin/<package>/       # Marketplace plugin packages (released independently)
└── lib/<library>/          # Internal shared libraries (bundled source-level into plugin artifacts, not published)
scripts/                    # Build factory and repository-level scripts (maintainer layer)
bazaar.json                 # Marketplace metadata templates for all plugin packages (source of name/url/author etc.)
docs/agents/                # Detailed build and release process documentation
```

## Local Development

1. Fork this repository
2. Clone your fork locally
3. Install mise-en-place
4. Install the tools via mise, such as node and pnpm (`mise install`)
5. Install dependencies via pnpm, or run the `mise deps install` command
6. Initialize lefthook by running `lefthook install` — already done if you ran `mise deps install`
7. Make your changes locally
8. Run `pnpm --filter <package> build` to build a single package, or `pnpm build` (i.e. `pnpm -r build`) to build all packages
9. Deploy a package to SiYuan for debugging: `mise run deploy -- -package <package_name>` (note the `--`; only arguments after it are passed to the script). Use `-target <workspace name>` to pick a workspace, or `-all` to deploy to all workspaces
10. Refresh SiYuan and confirm the plugin works under `SiYuan - Settings - Marketplace`

If you prefer not to use mise, install the dependencies listed in the project yourself and develop accordingly.

## Quality Gates

All of the following checks must pass before submitting (run at the repository root):

| Command                   | What it checks                                        |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `pnpm build`              | All packages build successfully                       |
| `pnpm lint`               | oxlint static analysis                                |
| `pnpm exec prettier -c .` | Code style                                            |
| `pnpm check`              | Per-package `meta.json` against marketplace contracts |
| `pnpm typecheck`          | Type checking for repository-level scripts            |

Packages with `.vue` sources (`siyuan-ignoreeditor`, `plugin-vscodelite-edit`) must additionally pass `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` within the package.

## Scope Conventions

1. A single pull request should focus on improvements or bug fixes for one package or shared library; changes spanning multiple packages or shared libraries should be submitted separately
2. Changes to package sources only do not touch the infrastructure layer; modifications to `scripts/`, `bazaar.json`, root workflows and other shared layers should be discussed in an issue first
3. **Do not edit `plugin.json` by hand** — it is a build artifact synthesized from the `bazaar.json` template and the package's `meta.json`; maintain versions in `meta.json`, and the `package.json` version is synced automatically by the pre-commit hook
4. When changing a package's behavior, keep its `AGENTS.md` (package-level conventions) up to date

## Commit and Pull Request Conventions

1. File an issue for features or bugs (use the issue templates: rewrite the title as prompted and tick the checklist honestly — issues that tick the "blindly check all" confirmation item are closed automatically by CI)
2. Submit a pull request for features or bugs
3. Commit messages must follow the Conventional Commits specification (`feat:` / `fix:` / `chore:` etc.) — the changelog is generated by git-cliff from commit messages
4. Committed code must pass the quality checks, including `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run format`, `pnpm run check`, `pnpm run typecheck`, etc.
5. By contributing code to this repository you agree to license it under the license used by the corresponding package or shared library, and agree that it may be relicensed under any license for any reason without separate notice in the future. Do not modify the license of the corresponding package or shared library due to your contribution.
